html:
Tsalaguwetiyi is the old homeland of the Cherokee in the southern Appalachian Mountains, across what is now western North Carolina, eastern Tennessee, north Georgia and nearby states. The Cherokee speak an Iroquoian language.

They lived in towns along the mountain rivers, each with a council house, and farmed maize, beans and squash. They grew out of the Mississippian world of mound-building towns. The army of Hernando de Soto passed through in 1540. Later the Cherokee traded deerskins with the English, and fought and dealt with the colonies and then the United States.

In 1821 Sequoyah created the Cherokee syllabary. Even so, in 1838 the US forced most Cherokee west on the Trail of Tears. Several hundred stayed in the North Carolina mountains, and their descendants form the Eastern Band of Cherokee Indians on the Qualla Boundary. See also Cherokee and Cherokee Nation.
